title: The lender logs a throttle delivered inside a 200 stream as a success
foundBy: session agent, answering a consumer's question about which kind of throttle its failed turns had met
details:
The lender records what an upstream answered from the status line and the headers, and it never reads a body. A provider can report a rate limit inside a `200` response stream, as a `response.failed` event whose error code is `rate_limit_exceeded`. The lender logs that call as `status=200`. It counts it as `ok`, and it prints no throttling warning.

This is the form codex retries, as measured for SBX-045, so it is the form a fleet at its limit is most likely to meet. For that fleet the lender's log and its per-slot summary still read as healthy, which is the gap SBX-046 set out to close.

To reproduce, arm `cs-sandbox lender fault <name> --status 200 --content-type text/event-stream --body-file <event>` with such an event, make a call, and read the lender's log. An injected answer is not logged as `answered` at all, so the same event has to come from a stub upstream to see the `status=200` line.

The lender's rule is that a stream passes through byte for byte and is never parsed. Watching the first bytes of an event stream for a failure event, without holding or changing them, may keep that rule. It needs a design before it is built.
